finding.claim: purge() calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any caller that reaches the handler can run purgeAll(). Compare rotateKeys, which correctly returns when mustPerm fails.
finding.source: Any authenticated (non-admin) user, or any request whose context carries a *User without the admin perm, sending a request to the purge route
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the requesting user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for a non-admin, but the return value is ignored

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm returns a bool and does not write a 403 or abort. The result is not used in an if statement. No other authorization check is present in the handler. No router or middleware is in the repo, so an upstream admin-gating middleware cannot be ruled out, but none is visible. The sibling handler rotateKeys uses mustPerm correctly, which shows the intended pattern. userFrom does an unchecked type assertion, so it panics if no user is in the context (a minor robustness issue, not an authorization bypass).

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12 returns a bool with no abort; no router/middleware in repo)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u,"admin") as a bare statement, discarding the bool, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user, unlike rotateKeys at handlers.go:33 which tests mustPerm; an upstream middleware can't be seen in this repo.

verdict_facts.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12 returns a bool and is called as a bare statement at :26; no 403/abort; no other check in the handler)
verdict_facts.reason: handlers.go:26 discards checkPerm's bool result, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any authenticated non-admin user, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm at handlers.go:33.
